title: Time-aware cost bucketization and canonical model-variant mart
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a canonical, queryable mart that attributes per-invocation cost to tenant + route + model_variant with time-aware bucketization logic. This mart will power Console dashboards, per-tenant billing checks, and nightly anomaly detection for cost regressions.

Scope and grain:
- Primary grain: invocation_id (one row per invocation) with derived daily/hourly aggregates.
- Aggregates: materialized daily rollups by tenant_id, route_id, model_variant_id, cost_bucket, and date.
- Cost buckets: compute token-cost and gpu-time cost and map to explicit buckets (e.g., micro, small, medium, large) based on configurable thresholds per tenant tier and model family. Buckets must be stable over time for historical comparability.

Canonicalization and model_variant mapping:
- Maintain a canonical model_variant dimension that unifies naming across hosted and dedicated runtimes and maps fallbacks (e.g., gpt-small-v2 -> gpt-small family). Proposed approach: SCD2 model for variant metadata so we can reconstruct historical attribution correctly when variant metadata changes.
- Build an enrichment pipeline that joins raw invocation events with model_variant dimension using fuzzy matching for legacy names and explicit mapping table for edge cases.

Temporal bucketing and retention:
- Time-aware bucketing: bucket thresholds can change over time per release; store bucket-versioning metadata and include bucket_version_id in mart rows.
- Partition strategy: daily partitioning on event_date + tenant_id micro-partition.
- Retention: keep invocation-level rows for 90 days, roll to compressed aggregate tables for 2 years.

Performance & storage design decisions:
- Use compact column encodings for variant_id and route_id (surrogate ints).
- Store precomputed token_cost and gpu_ms_cost at ingestion to avoid repeated unit-cost lookups.
- Materialize daily rollups as incremental ETL job (Spark/Dataproc) with idempotent upserts to avoid duplicate counts. For low-latency queries, provide a small set of pre-joined MV for top 100 tenants.

Backfill plan:
- Backfill historical 6 months via controlled job with checkpointing by date slice. Backfill will mark rows with original_ingestion_ts and backfill_run_id to assist validation.

Quality & validation:
- Build a suite of SQL-based tests: row-count reconciliation, cost-sum parity against billing pipeline, top-k tenant sanity checks.
- Add regression alert that compares daily per-tenant cost-per-invocation vs rolling baseline and fires when > 15% unexplained drift.

Query patterns expected:
- Per-tenant daily cost curves, per-model-variant trendlines, SLA/cost tradeoff panels in Console.
- Fast lookup by invocation_id for debugging customer support tickets.

Open design questions / trade-offs:
1) SCD1 vs SCD2 for model_variant: chosen SCD2 for auditability but increases storage and join complexity.
2) Materialized views vs nightly aggregate tables: MVs simpler but may not scale for largest tenants; implementing hybrid approach (MVs for small tenants, aggregates for large ones).
3) Bucket stability: we will version buckets and compute stable historical buckets, but this makes reclassification harder.

Deliverables:
- SQL DDL for canonical mart and supporting dimensions.
- Spark ETL job with idempotent upserts and backfill orchestration.
- Validation suite and reconciliation dashboards.
- Console dashboard widgets + docs.
